login.title: Sign in
login.heading: Sign in
mfa.title: Two-factor authentication
mfa.heading: Two-factor authentication
mfa.lostdevice: Lost your device? Enter one of your recovery codes instead.
mfa.securitykey: Use your security key or passkey
mfa.sms.number: Or have a code texted to you: your mobile number, with the country code
mfa.sms.sent: If that is the number on your account, a code is on its way.
devices.title: Remembered devices
devices.intro: When you sign in with your password on one of these, you are not asked for your second factor. Forget any you do not recognise.
emailotp.title: Email sign-in codes
emailotp.done.heading: Email codes are on
emailotp.done.body: You will be asked for a code from this address when you sign in.
emailotp.done.hint: This is the weakest of the second factors we offer, because account recovery already goes to your email — anybody with your mailbox can do both. An authenticator app or a passkey is stronger, and you can add one at any time.
emailotp.check.heading: Check your email
emailotp.start.body: We will send a code to this address each time you sign in.
emailotp.start.hint: An authenticator app is stronger: your email is also how your account is recovered, so a code sent there protects you from a stolen password but not from a stolen mailbox.
smsotp.title: Text message codes
smsotp.enrolled.note: A text message is the weakest second factor available here: moving a phone number to a new SIM needs no technical attack, only a convincing phone call to a mobile operator. An authenticator app or a passkey is stronger, and you can have both.
smsotp.sent: A code was sent to {Number}. Enter it to finish.
smsotp.verify.note: This factor is not active until the code comes back. That is what proves the number is yours and not a typo.
smsotp.number.label: Mobile number, with the country code
smsotp.number.note: Start with a + and the country code. Without it the number cannot be dialled, and guessing wrong sends your codes to somebody else.
smsotp.unavailable: Text messages are not available on this server.
smsotp.hashed: the number you gave, which is not kept: type it again to be sent a code
enrol.title: Set up two-factor authentication
enrol.scan: Scan this with your authenticator app:
enrol.typekey: Type this key into your authenticator app instead:
enrol.openlink: Or open this link on the device with your authenticator app.
enrol.intro: Use an authenticator app as a second step when you sign in. You will scan a code with the app, then enter the six digits it shows.
enrol.required: Your organisation requires a second factor on this account before you can continue.
enrol.keepscurrent: Your current authenticator keeps working until you confirm the new one.
recovery.title: Your recovery codes
recovery.heading: Two-factor authentication is on
recovery.save: Save these recovery codes now. Each one works once, and this is the only time they can be shown — only hashes are stored, so nobody can retrieve them for you later.
recovery.hint: Keep them somewhere other than the device with your authenticator app. If you lose both, you lose the account.
done.title: Password changed
done.heading: Your password has been changed
done.body: Every signed-in session was ended, on every device.
cancelled.title: Reset cancelled
cancelled.heading: That reset has been cancelled
cancelled.body: The link will not work. Nothing about your account has changed.
cancelled.hint: If you did not request the reset, your password is still safe, but somebody knows your address. Consider turning on two-factor authentication.
recover.title: Reset your password
recover.hint: We will email every address on the account, and the reset will only become usable after a short delay — so a request you did not make cannot go through without you having a chance to stop it.
sent.title: Check your email
sent.body: If an account matches what you entered, we have emailed reset instructions to every address on it.
sent.hint: The email includes a link to cancel, in case the request was not yours. Cancelling needs no sign-in.
reset.title: Choose a new password
reset.pending: This reset is not usable yet. It becomes available at {When} — about {Wait} from now.
reset.pending.hint: The wait is deliberate: it is the window in which a reset you did not ask for can still be cancelled from the link in your email.
reset.submit: Set password and sign out everywhere
passkeylink.title: Add a passkey
passkeylink.intro: This adds a passkey to {Account}, so you can sign in with your device's screen lock. The link works once, until {Until}.
passkeylink.needs: This needs a browser that supports passkeys, with JavaScript turned on.
passkeylink.done: Your passkey is saved, and this link no longer works.
passkeylink.invalid.hint: Ask your administrator for a new link. Each one works once, and a newer link replaces an older one.
changepw.title: Choose a new password
changepw.help: A few unrelated words make a password that is easy to remember and hard to guess. Length does more than symbols do.
signup.title: Create your account
signup.invitefixed: This invitation is for this address.
signup.passwordhint: At least 8 characters. You can add a passkey once you are in.
signupdone.title: Account created
signupdone.verify: The first time you sign in, we will send a code to {Email} to confirm the address is yours.
verifyemail.title: Confirm your email address
verifyemail.sent: We sent a six-digit code to {Address}. Enter it to finish signing in.
verifyemail.resent: Another code is on its way.
verifyemail.toosoon: A code was sent less than a minute ago. Check your inbox, or ask again shortly.
verifyemail.hint: A code works for ten minutes. Until the address is confirmed, this account cannot sign in.
verifyemail.closed: Too many wrong codes were entered, so this address can no longer be confirmed with a code. Reset your password from the link we email you instead: that confirms the address too.
logout.title: Sign out?
logout.heading: Sign out?
logout.body: An application asked to sign you out. Confirm that this is what you want.
fclogout.title: Signing out…
fclogout.heading: Signing you out

fclogout.progress.one: Signing you out of {n} application. This page will continue automatically.
fclogout.progress.other: Signing you out of {n} applications. This page will continue automatically.

backchannel.title: Sign-in requests
backchannel.intro: An application has asked to sign in as you. Approve it only if you started it.
backchannel.binding: Reference shown on the other device:
consent.title: Authorize {Client}
consent.heading: {Client} wants access to your account
consent.operation: And to perform this specific operation:
device.title: Connect a device
device.done.heading: Device connected
device.done.body: You can put this away and go back to the device.
device.denied.heading: Request refused
device.denied.body: Nothing was granted. If you did not start this, somebody else may have asked you to enter that code — it is worth telling whoever runs your systems.
device.confirm.heading: Allow this device?
device.confirm.body: {ClientName} is asking to sign in as you on a device.
device.confirm.warning: Only continue if you started this yourself, on a device in front of you. Nobody legitimate will ask you to enter a code they sent you.
device.enter: Enter the code shown on your device.
connected.title: Connected applications
connected.none: No application has been granted access to your account.
sessions.title: Your sessions
sessions.none: You have no other active sessions.
sessions.how.mfa: Signed in with a password and a second factor
sessions.how.multifactor: Signed in with more than one factor
sessions.endcurrent: End this session (signs you out here)
accountpw.title: Change your password
accountpw.endsothers: Changing your password ends every session, so you will sign in again with the new one.
reccodes.title: Recovery codes
reccodes.nofactor: Recovery codes back up a second factor, and you have not set one up yet.

reccodes.remaining.zero: You have no unused recovery codes left.
reccodes.remaining.one: You have {n} unused recovery code left.
reccodes.remaining.other: You have {n} unused recovery codes left.

reccodes.explain: Each code works once. Keep them somewhere other than the device with your authenticator app.
reccodes.replaces: Generating new codes cancels your current ones, so any you have written down will stop working.
portal.title: Your applications
portal.empty: No applications have been set up yet.
portal.empty.hint: An administrator registers one with signari client create.
portal.nolaunch: You can use this, but no launch address is configured. Ask an administrator to set -launch-url.
portal.blocked.heading: Not available to you
portal.blocked.hint: Listed with the reason, so you know what to ask for rather than having to open a ticket to find out.
account.title: Your account
account.heading: Sign-in methods
account.note: Adding a provider here is the only way to link one to this account. We never link on a matching email address alone.
account.none: No external sign-in providers are configured.
emailchange.title: Email address
emailchange.hint: A code goes to the new address, and the account moves to it only when the code comes back. Until then nothing changes, and once it does the old address is told.
emailchange.sent: We sent a code to {NewAddress}. Enter it to move your account there.
emailchange.done: Your account now uses the new address, and it is verified.
emailchange.closed: Too many wrong codes were entered for this address, so it can no longer be confirmed. Keep your current address, or try a different one.
error.emailchange.address: Enter the full address you want to use.
profile.title: Your profile
profile.none: Your organisation keeps nothing about you here that you can see.
security.title: Sign-in methods
security.intro: Every way you can prove it is you, beyond your password.
security.sms.hashed: A number kept only as a hash
security.switchedoff: Switched off after too many wrong codes
security.recovery.none: Made once you have a second factor
security.hint: Removing a method asks you to have signed in recently, and you are told by email and text message whenever one is added or removed. Removing your last second factor removes your recovery codes too.
security.removed: Removed. You have been told by email as well.
security.removed.recovery: Removed. It was your last second factor, so your recovery codes have gone too.
account.passkeys.none: No passkeys yet. A passkey signs you in with your device's screen lock instead of a password.
account.passkey.name: Name
racindex.title: Remote access
racindex.notconfigured: Remote access is not configured on this server. No SIGNARI_GUACD_ADDR is set, so nothing can be connected to.
racindex.none: There are no machines you can reach.
racindex.none.hint: If you expect to see something here, ask an administrator whether the connection requires a group you are not in.
umaclaims.title: Confirm this request
umaclaims.heading: {ClientName} is asking on your behalf
umaclaims.note: Confirming tells {ResourceServer} who you are. It does not grant access on its own: whoever owns this decides that.
err.title: Sign-in error
federr.title: Sign-in could not be completed
samlerr.title: Sign-in request refused
samlerr.heading: This sign-in request was refused
reason.breached: Your password has appeared in a known data breach since you chose it, so it needs to be changed before you continue.
reason.migratedbreach: The password you brought from your previous provider appears in a known data breach, so it needs to be changed before you continue.
reason.administrator: An administrator has asked you to choose a new password.
scope.offline_access: Stay signed in and access your account while you are away
error.totp.mismatch: That code did not match. Check your authenticator app and try again.
error.totp.expired: That setup code has expired. Start again to get a new one.
error.totp.fips: Authenticator apps cannot be added here yet: this organisation uses SHA-1 codes, which this server's FIPS mode refuses. Ask your administrator to choose SHA-256, or add a passkey instead.
error.reset.expired: That link is not valid or has expired.
error.passkeylink.invalid: This link has been used, has expired or was never issued.
error.verifyemail.mismatch: That code is not right, or it has expired.
error.verifyemail.unsent: The code could not be sent just now. Try sending another.
error.invite.invalid: That invitation link is not valid. It may have been used already, or expired. Ask whoever invited you for a new one.
error.captcha.incomplete: That challenge was not completed. Please try again.
bridge.title: Signing you in…
bridge.noscript: JavaScript is disabled. Continue to complete signing in.
mail.signincode.subject: Your sign-in code
mail.confirmaddress.subject: Confirm this address for sign-in codes
mail.recovery.requested.subject: Password reset requested
mail.recovery.requested.body:
Someone asked to reset the password for your account.

If this was you, the reset becomes available in {Wait}:

  {ResetURL}

If it was NOT you, cancel it now -- no sign-in needed:

  {CancelURL}

The delay is deliberate. It exists so that a reset you did not ask for cannot happen without you having a chance to stop it.

This message was sent to every address on the account, including ones the request did not come from.
sms.recovery.requested: A password reset was requested on your account. If this was not you, check your email now for a one-tap link to cancel it -- no sign-in needed.
mail.password.changed.subject: Your password was changed
mail.password.changed.body:
Your account password has just been changed, and every signed-in session was ended.

If this was not you, reset it again immediately and contact your administrator.
sms.password.changed: Your account password was just changed and all sessions ended. If this was not you, reset it again now and contact your administrator.
mail.password.set.subject: An administrator set a new password for your account
mail.password.set.body:
An administrator set a new password for your account, and every signed-in session was ended.

If you expected this, sign in with the password you were given; you may be asked to choose your own.

If you did not, contact your administrator.
sms.password.set: An administrator set a new password for your account and ended all sessions. If you did not expect this, contact them.
mail.smsotp.enrolled.subject: Sign-in codes will now be sent by text message
mail.smsotp.enrolled.body:
A phone number was just set up as a second sign-in step for your account, and sign-in codes will be texted to it.

If you did this, there is nothing to do.

If you did NOT, someone else may have access to your account: sign in, remove the number from your sign-in methods and change your password.
sms.smsotp.enrolled: This number now receives sign-in codes for your account. If this was not you, sign in and remove it, then change your password.
mail.federation.linked.subject: {Provider} can now sign you in
mail.federation.linked.body:
Your {Provider} account was just linked to your account here, and can now be used to sign in.

If you did this, there is nothing to do.

If you did NOT, someone else may have access to your account: sign in, remove {Provider} from your account page and change your password.
sms.federation.linked: {Provider} was just linked to your account and can now sign you in. If this was not you, sign in and remove it.
mail.federation.unlinked.subject: {Provider} can no longer sign you in
mail.federation.unlinked.body:
Your {Provider} account was just unlinked from your account here, and can no longer be used to sign in.

If you did not do this, sign in and check your account page, and change your password.
sms.federation.unlinked: {Provider} was just unlinked from your account. If this was not you, sign in and change your password.
mail.email.changed.self.subject: Your account moved to a new email address
mail.email.changed.self.body:
The email address on your account was just changed, after a code sent to the new address was entered. Messages about your account now go there.

If you did this, there is nothing to do.

If you did NOT, someone else may have access to your account: contact your administrator now, since resetting the password now goes to the new address.
sms.email.changed.self: The email address on your account was just changed. If this was not you, contact your administrator now.
mail.email.changed.subject: The email address on your account was changed
mail.email.changed.body:
An administrator changed the email address on your account. Messages about your account now go to the new address, which is not verified until a message sent to it comes back.

If you did not ask for this, contact your administrator.
sms.email.changed: The email address on your account was changed by an administrator. If you did not ask for this, contact them.
mail.passkey.added.subject: A new passkey was added to your account
mail.passkey.added.body:
A passkey named {Label} was added to your account on {When}.

If you added it, there is nothing to do.

If you did NOT add it, someone else may have had access to your account. Sign in, remove the passkey you do not recognise, and change your password. If you cannot sign in, contact support at {Support}.
sms.passkey.added: A new passkey ({Label}) was just added to your account. If this was not you, sign in and remove it, then change your password.
mail.passkey.removed.subject: A passkey was removed from your account
mail.passkey.removed.body:
The passkey {Label} was removed from your account on {When}.

If you removed it, there is nothing to do.

If you did NOT remove it, someone else may have access to your account. Sign in, check the passkeys listed there, and change your password. If you cannot sign in, contact support at {Support}.
sms.passkey.removed: The passkey {Label} was just removed from your account. If this was not you, sign in and change your password.
mail.recoverycodes.replaced.subject: Your recovery codes were replaced
mail.recoverycodes.replaced.body:
Your account's recovery codes were just regenerated. The previous set no longer works.

If you did not do this, someone else may have access to your account: change your password and review your sign-in methods.
sms.recoverycodes.replaced: Your account's recovery codes were just replaced. If this was not you, change your password now.
mail.totp.enrolled.subject: An authenticator app was set up on your account
mail.totp.enrolled.body:
An authenticator app was just set up as a second sign-in step for your account.

If you did this, there is nothing to do.

If you did NOT, someone else may have access to your account: sign in, review your sign-in methods, and change your password.
sms.totp.enrolled: An authenticator app was just set up on your account. If this was not you, sign in and review your sign-in methods.
mail.factor.removed.subject: A sign-in method was removed from your account
mail.factor.removed.body:
An administrator removed a sign-in method from your account: {Factor}. You have been signed out everywhere.

Your next sign-in may ask you to set up a new one. If you did not ask for this, contact your administrator.
sms.factor.removed: An administrator removed a sign-in method ({Factor}) from your account and signed you out. If you did not ask for this, contact them.
mail.factor.removed.self.subject: A sign-in method was removed from your account
mail.factor.removed.self.body:
A sign-in method was removed from your account: {Factor}.

If you removed it, there is nothing to do.

If you did not, someone else may be signed in to your account. Sign in, change your password, and check your sign-in methods and devices.
sms.factor.removed.self: A sign-in method ({Factor}) was removed from your account. If this was not you, sign in and change your password.
mail.factor.assigned.subject: A security token was added to your account
mail.factor.assigned.body:
An administrator made a hardware token the second step of your sign-in. It replaces any authenticator app you had.

If you did not ask for this, contact your administrator.
mail.verifyemail.subject: Your code to confirm this address
mail.verifyemail.body:
Your code is {Code}. Enter it on the sign-in page to confirm this address is yours. It works for ten minutes.

If you did not create an account, you can ignore this message: nobody can sign in to it until the code is entered.
mail.passkeylink.subject: Add a passkey to your account
mail.passkeylink.body:
An administrator sent you a link to add a passkey to your account, so you can sign in with your device's screen lock:

  {URL}

It works once, until {Until}. Do not forward it: whoever opens it can add a passkey to your account.

If you did not expect this, do not open it, and contact your administrator.
sms.factor.assigned: An administrator added a hardware token to your account. If you did not ask for this, contact them.
mail.totp.replaced.subject: Your authenticator app was replaced
mail.totp.replaced.body:
The authenticator app used as your second sign-in step was just replaced. The previous one no longer works.

If you did not do this, someone else may have access to your account: change your password and review your sign-in methods.
sms.totp.replaced: Your authenticator app was just replaced. If this was not you, change your password now.
mail.totp.disabled.subject: Your authenticator app was switched off after too many wrong codes
mail.totp.disabled.body:
Too many wrong codes in a row were entered for the authenticator app on your account, so it has been switched off and its codes are no longer accepted.

Only someone who already entered your password can reach that step. If it was not you, change your password now.

To sign in, use a recovery code or another sign-in method, then set the authenticator app up again. If you have no other way in, contact your administrator.
sms.totp.disabled: Your authenticator app was switched off after too many wrong codes. If this was not you, change your password now.
mail.recoverycodes.disabled.subject: Your recovery codes were switched off after too many wrong attempts
mail.recoverycodes.disabled.body:
Too many wrong recovery codes in a row were entered for your account, so your recovery codes have been switched off and none of them is accepted any more.

Only someone who already entered your password can reach that step. If it was not you, change your password now.

To sign in, use another sign-in method, then generate a new set of recovery codes. If you have no other way in, contact your administrator.
sms.recoverycodes.disabled: Your recovery codes were switched off after too many wrong attempts. If this was not you, change your password now.
mail.emailotp.enrolled.subject: Sign-in codes will now be sent by email
mail.emailotp.enrolled.body:
Email was just set up as a second sign-in step for your account, and sign-in codes will go to the address that was confirmed.

If you did this, there is nothing to do.

If you did NOT, someone else may have access to your account: sign in, review your sign-in methods, and change your password.
sms.emailotp.enrolled: Email was just set up as a second sign-in step on your account. If this was not you, sign in and review your sign-in methods.
mail.emailotp.moved.subject: Sign-in codes will no longer come to this address
mail.emailotp.moved.body:
The second sign-in step on your account was just moved to a different email address. Codes will no longer be sent here.

If you did this, there is nothing to do.

If you did NOT, someone else has access to your account and has taken over your sign-in codes. Change your password now and contact your administrator.
sms.smsotp.moved: Sign-in codes for your account will no longer be texted to this number: they were just moved to another one. If this was not you, change your password now and contact your administrator.
mail.emailotp.disabled.subject: Email sign-in codes were switched off after too many wrong codes
mail.emailotp.disabled.body:
Too many wrong codes in a row were entered for the email sign-in step on your account, so it has been switched off and no more codes will be sent or accepted.

Only someone who already entered your password can reach that step. If it was not you, change your password now.

To sign in, use a recovery code or another sign-in method, then set up email codes again. If you have no other way in, contact your administrator.
sms.emailotp.disabled: Email sign-in codes on your account were switched off after too many wrong codes. If this was not you, change your password now.
mail.smsotp.disabled.subject: Text message sign-in codes were switched off after too many wrong codes
mail.smsotp.disabled.body:
Too many wrong codes in a row were entered for the text message sign-in step on your account, so it has been switched off and no more codes will be sent or accepted.

Only someone who already entered your password can reach that step. If it was not you, change your password now.

To sign in, use a recovery code or another sign-in method, then set up text message codes again. If you have no other way in, contact your administrator.
sms.smsotp.disabled: Text message sign-in codes on your account were switched off after too many wrong codes. If this was not you, change your password now.
